guide.q.create_listing: How do I create a listing?
guide.a.create_listing:
A listing is one thing you sell — a workshop, a meal, a room, anything people can book. From the Listings page, click Add Listing.

Give your listing a name, set how many people can book, and choose which contact details to collect. You can collect email, phone, postal address, and special instructions — any mix, or none at all. Leave the price blank if it is free.

Once it exists, share the booking link with your attendees.
guide.q.setup_payments: How do I set up payments?
guide.a.setup_payments:
To take card payments you need an account with a payment company. This site works with three: Stripe, Square, and SumUp. They take a slice of each payment as their fee, and pay the rest into your bank account. Signing up is free. You give your bank details, and approval can take a day or two.

Once you have an account, go to Settings, choose your payment company, and paste in your key. A key is a long password that lets this site talk to that company.

For Stripe and SumUp, everything else is set up for you. For Square, you also copy the webhook address shown on the page into your Square account — see the Payments section below for the full steps.
guide.a.what_is_dashboard:
The Listings page is your dashboard. It lists all your listings with attendee counts, booking links, and quick buttons.

At the top, the Active Listing Statistics section shows totals across all your open listings: total income, number of ticket rows, and total attendees. Click the heading to open or close it.
guide.q.test_after_changing_settings: Should I test after changing settings?
guide.a.test_after_changing_settings:
Yes. After you change any setting — especially payments, listing limits, or booking fields — make a test booking from start to finish. That way you catch problems before your attendees do.

Create a test listing, or use test payment details, and book it all the way through.
guide.q.report_bug: How do I report a bug?
guide.a.report_bug:
This project is new (started January 2026), so some things will not work right yet.

If something behaves wrongly, email hello@chobble.com. Say what you did, what happened, and what you expected instead. The more detail you give, the faster it can be fixed.
guide.a.contact_support:
The Support page sends a message straight to the team who run your site. Describe what you need help with and send it. Replies come back by email.

After you send, a short reminder appears. It asks you to wait for the answer rather than sending the same message again.
guide.q.support_page_availability: Why don't I see a Support page?
guide.a.support_page_availability: The Support page appears only when the people who run your site have switched it on and given a contact address. If there is no Support link in your menu, contact them the way you normally would.
